title: Local Shell & Filesystem Administration
purpose: Complete useful local foundations with real startup, history, editor, link, search and access evidence. Ten independent practice lessons; recommended order is guidance, not an unlock system.
prerequisites: Existing Bash, paths, quoting, permissions and users/groups practice. Read the declared scope before guest sudo; no host commands or account/security changes.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 limited practice and reinforcement of 103.1/3/6/8, 104.5/6/7, 105.1 and 110.1. Self-reviewed, unscored, not full objective coverage or LPI endorsement.

objectives: 104.6 /104.7 /105.1 reinforcement — narrow real-guest practice; completion is self-reviewed.
troubleshooting: Editing the initial hard link would alter the protected source.
A checksum passing does not prove independent inode or narrow mode.
Do not delete stale evidence merely to make the directory look clean.
cleanup: Re-establish only the recorded lesson workspace/identity variables and guards after reopening. This command checks exact members and expected types before deleting known files. It is a cooperative practice guard, not protection against guest root or concurrent hostile substitution.

clean_local() { here || return 19; extra=$(find -P . -mindepth 1 ! \( -path './links/current' -o -path './records/source.txt' -o -path './original.sha256' -o -path './original.meta' -o -path './stale.txt' -o -path './handover.txt' -o -path './report.txt' -o -path './links' -o -path './records' \) -print -quit) || return 19; test -z "$extra" || return 19; test -d links && test ! -L links || return 19; test -d records && test ! -L records || return 19; test -L links/current || return 19; test -f records/source.txt && test ! -L records/source.txt || return 19; test -f original.sha256 && test ! -L original.sha256 || return 19; test -f original.meta && test ! -L original.meta || return 19; test -f stale.txt && test ! -L stale.txt || return 19; test -f handover.txt && test ! -L handover.txt || return 19; test -f report.txt && test ! -L report.txt || return 19; rm -- links/current records/source.txt original.sha256 original.meta stale.txt handover.txt report.txt || return 19; rmdir -- links records || return 19; cd "$HOME" && rmdir -- "$w"; }; clean_local
If refusal occurs, inspect and retain the workspace. Confirmed Reset retains the old disk; never use recursive deletion or adopt a foreign path.
materials: Start a unique workspace and define accident guards: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-handover.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-handover.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here

Mutations stay inside the recorded w; sticky additionally permits its unique /tmp/ll-sticky.* directory. Priority includes read-only /usr/bin audit and /proc identity queries for its owned bounded task. No account, authentication, sudo policy or package changes.
Challenge has independent outcomes, not an automatically scored transcript. Record the workspace before closing; Resume does not preserve RAM, shell variables or jobs.

Trusted initial exercise fixture (not the repair): here && fresh records links original.sha256 original.meta unsafe-copy.txt stale.txt && { mkdir records links; printf 'approved handover\n' > records/source.txt; chmod 0640 records/source.txt; sha256sum records/source.txt > original.sha256; stat -c '%a %h' records/source.txt > original.meta; ln -s ../missing.txt links/current; ln records/source.txt unsafe-copy.txt; printf 'obsolete path: missing.txt\n' > stale.txt; }
observations: Retain actual commands, exit status and output for the Challenge outcomes.
Record what an incorrect attempt demonstrates and what remains uncertain.
questions: Which observations prove the requested outcome rather than merely successful execution?
What would change outside this bounded exercise?
limitations: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 104.6 /104.7 /105.1 reinforcement. Self-reviewed and unscored: the application does not inspect guest results. No full-objective or exam-readiness claim.
